name: tamirs-superpowers-guard
description: In-process guard for tamirs-superpowers: holds a destructive shell command (force push, rm -rf, git reset --hard, ...) until you answer Proceed or Cancel, and refuses a file write in the main checkout while an orchestration objective is active. Companion to the core plugin; Claude Code and Claude Desktop only.

hold_destructive_commands.title: Hold destructive shell commands until you answer
hold_destructive_commands.description: On by default. A Bash call that force-pushes, deletes a branch with -D, removes a worktree with --force, resets --hard, cleans with -f, runs rm -rf outside a temp directory, or discards the working tree (git checkout -- . / git restore .) pauses in a Proceed/Cancel dialog before it runs. Cancel refuses the call with the guard's reason. Where nothing can draw the dialog (claude -p, the SDK) the call goes through unheld.

deny_main_checkout_writes.title: Refuse main-checkout writes while an objective is active
deny_main_checkout_writes.description: On by default. While an orchestration objective is active (SUPERPOWERS_OBJECTIVE_ID, or an objective.json with status active under .dev-files/objectives/) and the session sits in the main checkout rather than a worktree, an Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit of a file inside the repository is refused with the objective's worktrees named. Writes under .dev-files/ and inside any agent worktree pass. The in-process mirror of hooks/enforce-worktree-edits.sh, which stays canonical.
